text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I've attached the rent notice I received from the Rebhalde Cooperative at the end of June.

My lease, which I signed in December 2022, is a bit of a muddle. On one page there is a table saying the rent goes up by fixed amounts on certain dates. Whether this particular increase is one of those steps, I honestly can't work out. My friend Nina Fankhauser, who read the contract with me, is fairly sure it is, because the date matches the table. When I asked Mr Felix Frei, he said the table was "no longer relevant" but wouldn't explain why. So that part is still a mystery.

What I do know is that the lease also contains a clause tying the rent to the Swiss consumer price index, and as far as I understand, this increase applies that index clause.

The notice, dated 29 June 2026, tells me my rent for the flat at Rosenweg 54 in Wohlen will go from CHF 3270 to CHF 3350 a month from 1 October 2026. For our household that is a noticeable jump on top of everything else getting more expensive.

Could you help me understand whether this is correct, and whether it matters if it's an index increase or one of the steps from the table? I'd like to know if I should contest it before any deadline runs out.

Thank you,
Emma Brunner
